program: Hi Code Product-Grade Desktop and Industrial Workbench

risks.title: Assistant output is not yet fully protocol-native
risks.impact: Concurrent desktop sessions can remain coupled to compatibility output capture, limiting reliable replay and SDK parity.
risks.mitigation: RuntimeEventSink, assistant delta/completed events, Electron/CLI/TUI adapters, concurrency isolation, and stdout-disabled real Electron acceptance are implemented in HC-RUN-201.
risks.trigger: Any output mixing, blank response, or transcript mismatch blocks release promotion.

risks.title: Full model context depended on legacy session JSON
risks.impact: A missing or stale legacy session snapshot could make a durable conversation read-only or silently lose assistant and tool context after a crash.
risks.mitigation: HC-RUN-202 persists exact hidden system/user/assistant/tool messages, reconstructs complete context from typed records or protocol JSONL, preserves legacy files, and verifies stale-snapshot crash recovery and idempotent import.
risks.trigger: Any resumable thread that loses tool-call semantics, duplicates records, or prefers a stale snapshot reopens this risk.

risks.title: Interrupted turns require side-effect-aware recovery
risks.impact: A blind retry can duplicate a tool side effect, reuse stale approval, or overwrite a complete assistant answer.
risks.mitigation: HC-RUN-203 records approval decisions, preserves bounded partial output, restores the source session before safe retries, and blocks replay when a side-effecting tool is complete or has unknown state.
risks.trigger: Any automatic retry after unknown or completed mutating work, reused approval, or interrupted turn presented as completed reopens this risk.

risks.title: No real Electron responsive E2E baseline
risks.impact: Unit and renderer smoke tests can miss clipping, unreachable controls, window lifecycle, and preload integration regressions.
risks.mitigation: Playwright now launches the production Electron entrypoint at 720/1024/1440 widths locally and under Linux/Xvfb CI, with real navigation, drawer, overflow, and page-error assertions.
risks.trigger: A core action hidden without an alternative or a failed real Electron launch blocks release.

risks.title: Electron compatibility line needs an isolated supported-version upgrade
risks.impact: Runtime support and Chromium security maintenance can age before stable release.
risks.mitigation: HC-PLAT-110 pins Electron 43.1.0, validates the Chromium 150 / Node 24 embedded runtime and security flags, confirms no native production add-on, generates the macOS alpha DMG, and records passing Linux/macOS/Windows startup smoke from GitHub Actions run 29116173672.
risks.trigger: Unsupported Electron status or a high production/runtime advisory blocks release.

risks.title: Desktop installers are not commercially signed
risks.impact: macOS Gatekeeper or Windows SmartScreen can warn users and weaken installation trust.
risks.mitigation: Keep artifacts prerelease-only, publish checksums, and require signing identities before stable promotion.
risks.trigger: Stable release or automatic update enablement requires valid signing and platform smoke evidence.

risks.title: Model transport lacks an explicit capability contract
risks.impact: A model request can reach the network before Hi Code discovers that images, tool streaming, structured output, reasoning, or token limits are unsupported, and provider-specific errors lose stable semantics.
risks.mitigation: HC-PROV-210 delivers a separate Model Provider Adapter registry, fail-fast capability negotiation, normalized events/errors/usage, stable tool correlation, Runtime Protocol projection, and a real local-SSE compatibility migration for current model profiles.
risks.trigger: Any unsupported requirement sent to a provider, silent capability downgrade, or provider event that cannot be normalized blocks alpha.9.

risks.title: Responses and Chat Completions semantics can diverge during migration
risks.impact: Incorrect event mapping can duplicate tool calls, lose image inputs or usage, report an interrupted request as complete, or silently move existing compatible endpoints to an unsupported protocol.
risks.mitigation: HC-PROV-211 keeps Chat Completions as the compatibility default, makes Responses selection explicit, and verifies both transports with real local HTTP streams and shared Runtime tool-loop tests.
risks.trigger: Any implicit protocol migration, duplicate or incomplete tool lifecycle, lost usage, image mismatch, or false terminal state blocks HC-PROV-211 completion.

risks.title: Anthropic and Ollama wire semantics can be silently flattened
risks.impact: Tool identities, image encoding, stop reasons, usage, interruption, or provider-specific reasoning metadata could be lost or misreported when mapped into the shared runtime.
risks.mitigation: HC-PROV-212 implements dedicated adapters with explicit profile protocols, bounded real loopback stream fixtures, capability preflight, strict event ordering, unchanged legacy defaults, and a reviewed boundary that discards raw thinking instead of relabeling it.
risks.trigger: Any implicit protocol switch, untyped provider field, duplicate tool completion, false terminal state, or unsupported capability sent over the network blocks HC-PROV-212 completion.

risks.title: Industrial bridge capabilities can be overstated
risks.impact: Users could mistake plans or templates for licensed commercial-tool execution.
risks.mitigation: Preserve simulated, not_run, external_required, and manual approval evidence through UI, gates, and releases.
risks.trigger: Any bridge or dry-run result displayed as real/passed is a release blocker.

risks.title: User shell profile references a removed ComfyUI environment
risks.impact: Bash test and user-command output contains a benign startup warning that can obscure relevant diagnostics.
risks.mitigation: Repair or guard the external profile entry outside the repository; do not change project tests to hide it.
risks.trigger: If the warning changes command exit status or masks tool output, treat it as a developer-environment blocker.

risks.title: Program evidence was previously ignored or historical
risks.impact: Old issue counts or untracked pass claims could be mistaken for current release evidence.
risks.mitigation: Track program/task/evidence paths, mark old audits historical, and capture hashed command logs.
risks.trigger: A release claim without source-linked committed evidence reopens this risk.
